Exercise: Narrow Stance Leg Press

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- push

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- machine

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
ATP-PC system and glycolytic pathway

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- hamstring_engagement
- quadriceps_hypertrophy
- glute_activation
- calves_strengthening

Contraindications:

- Recent knee surgery or injury
- Severe knee pain or instability

Exercise Variations:

- name: Narrow Stance Leg Press with Bands, equipment: machine and resistance bands
- name: Narrow Stance Leg Press with Chains, equipment: machine and weight chains

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Close-Grip Squats, equipment: barbell or dumbbells
- exercise_name: Single-Leg Bulgarian Split Squats, equipment: dumbbells or barbell

Instructions:

- Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a less-than-shoulder-width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Your feet should be around 3 inches or less apart. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.
- Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not lock your knees. Your torso and the legs should make a perfect 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.
- As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
- Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.
